# `mlkem` — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 1 · S1 E1 A1 H1 P1 *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** ahead — OpenSSL 3.5.5 libcrypto ML-KEM, against mlkem-native 2.0.0 / AWS-LC 5.12, Go 1.27 `crypto/mlkem`, BoringSSL, RustCrypto `ml-kem` 0.3, libcrux-ml-kem and Zig std (surveyed 2026-11-01; gaps closed 2026-11-01: seed-form private key, keygen pairwise consistency test, error-returning entropy failure)

**Ahead:** speed — 0.48–0.76× aws-lc-rs 1.18.0 (AWS-LC / mlkem-native AVX2 assembly) on keygen, encaps and decaps for all three parameter sets, in portable Zig (measured 2026-11-01)

**Audit:** review 2026-11-01 · mutation 2026-11-01 (138/148, 10 eq) · src 07ad2d26a5d63cc5

Audit detail: the review is an independent read-only pass over poly, sample, keccak4 and kem against FIPS 203 (bounds, Montgomery bookkeeping, constant time, conformance, zeroisation, API hazards; 0 HIGH, its MEDIUMs fixed the same day); the mutation run is 148 schemata mutants over the four library files, 138 killed (3 by tests it added), 10 argued equivalent (redundant `reduce` before a bounded consumer, Compress₁ symmetry, masks wider than their operand).

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-01 (960,000 runs clean, MLKEM_FUZZ, 8 jobs × 40,000 × 3 sets, every reach label hit; std as the differential oracle) · ct 2026-11-01 (ctgrind keygen/encaps/decaps × 3 sets: d‖z, m, dk and the ciphertext tainted, 0 in-file; ρ declassified as public) · panic 2026-11-01 (blind review of every pub entry point: no arithmetic or index panic reachable; the entropy abort of std's infallible `generate`/`encaps` shape has `tryGenerate`/`tryEncaps` twins; keccak4's length asserts moved to comptime)

**Performance:** ref 0.18–0.29× OpenSSL 3.5.5 libcrypto (keygen, encaps, decaps × 3 sets) · fastest 0.76× aws-lc-rs 1.18.0 (measured 2026-11-01)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

**Where we are ahead:** speed (faster than AWS-LC's assembly on every row, without assembly);
all three parameter sets with both the seed and the expanded private-key form (Go and BoringSSL
have neither 512 nor expanded import; mlkem-native/libcrux have no seed form). **Where we are

number; no ASN.1 key encodings (belong to `pkcs8`/`x509`, Backlog).

## What this module is, and what it is not

ML-KEM (FIPS 203, 2024-08-13): KeyGen, Encaps and Decaps for ML-KEM-512/768/1024, the K-PKE
underneath, the §7.2 encapsulation-key and §7.3 decapsulation-key input checks, the seed-form
private key (d ‖ z, 64 bytes) and the expanded FIPS 203 form, and an optional FIPS 140-3 pairwise
consistency test. Pure Zig; allocation-free.

Not here: Kyber round 3 / draft00 (refused — superseded; std still has `d00` if anyone needs it);
hybrid combiners and X-Wing (they live in `hpke` and `tls13`, which depend on this module, not the
other way round); ASN.1 / PKCS#8 / SPKI encodings of ML-KEM keys (deferred to `pkcs8`/`x509`).

## Algorithm

FIPS 203 Algorithms 13–18 exactly; the internal representation differs from the spec's only in
the NTT-domain coefficient order (below), which is undone at every encoding boundary, so every
byte string the API produces or consumes is FIPS 203's.

- **Ring arithmetic** (`poly.zig`): 256 `i16` coefficients as sixteen `@Vector(16, i16)`.
  Montgomery multiplication with R = 2^16 (`mulhi` pairs, q^-1 = −3327), Barrett reduction to
  [0, q] (`mulhi` by 20159, shift 10), conditional subtraction to [0, q) before any encoding.
  Zetas: 17^BitRev7(i) · R mod q, centred (the pq-crystals table, pinned by a test).
- **NTT layout.** Layers len = 128…16 are whole-vector butterflies with a broadcast zeta; the
  last three (8, 4, 2) pair lanes inside a 32-coefficient block through AVX2-native splits
  (128-bit halves, 64-bit and 32-bit interleaves), each its own inverse. The result is then
  stored deinterleaved per block — even entries (constant terms of the 16 degree-1 residues),
  then odd — so `baseMulAcc` (Algorithm 11/12) is lane-wise. `ntt_pos` maps FIPS order to it.
  Bounds: inputs |a| < q, seven unreduced layers < 8q < 2^15; `baseMulAcc` adds < 2q per call,
  reduced after at most k = 4 calls; the inverse NTT Barrett-reduces each sum and ends with
  f = R²/128, which cancels the R^-1 of the base multiplication.
- **Sampling** (`sample.zig`, `keccak4.zig`): SampleNTT over SHAKE128(ρ ‖ j ‖ i) for Â[i][j]
  (ρ ‖ i ‖ j for the cached Âᵀ), four matrix entries per 4-way Keccak call, three blocks squeezed
  then one at a time per batch; rejection is branch-free per candidate. PRF_η = SHAKE256(s ‖ N),
  noise polynomials four per call; CBD η = 2 / 3 by bit-sliced popcounts.
- **Compression**: Compress_d(x) = ((x·2^d + 1664) · ⌈2^36/q⌉) >> 36 mod 2^d, exact for every
  x < q and d ∈ {1, 4, 5, 10, 11} (exhaustive test), packed in byte-aligned groups.
- **KEM**: G = SHA3-512, H = SHA3-256, J = SHAKE256 (std). Decaps re-encrypts and selects K′ or
  J(z ‖ c) with a mask hidden from the optimiser by an empty `asm` barrier.

## Constant-time contract

Secret: the seed d ‖ z, σ, s, e, the encapsulation randomness m and r, y, e1, e2, the decrypted
m′, the decapsulation key, the shared secret. Every operation on them — CBD, NTT, base
multiplication, compression, the message encoding, the Fujisaki–Okamoto comparison and select — is
branch-free and index-free in the data. **Not constant-time, by design:** SampleNTT's rejection
loop length, which depends only on ρ (public: it is the last 32 bytes of ek); the §7.3 hash
comparison in `SecretKey.fromBytes` (over public data).

Machine-checked by `scripts/checks/ctgrind.sh mlkem` (rows in `scripts/checks/ctgrind-expected.tsv`,
ReleaseFast): keygen with d ‖ z tainted, encaps with m tainted, decaps with dk and the ciphertext
tainted, all three sets — 0 in-file contexts each; ρ is declassified inside KeyGen (`kem.zig`),
the one place where a public value is derived from the secret seed.

Zeroisation: secret intermediates (noise vectors, m, K ‖ r, the SHA-3/SHAKE states, the
re-encryption) are wiped with `secureZero` before return; values returned to the caller
(`KeyPair`, `SecretKey`, shared secrets) are the caller's to wipe.

## Limits and refusals

Fixed-size APIs: every key, ciphertext and seed is a `[N]u8` of the FIPS 203 length, so length
errors are type errors. `PublicKey.fromBytes` rejects any t̂ coefficient ≥ q
(`error.NonCanonical`, FIPS 203 §7.2; all 2592 CCTV modulus vectors pinned).
`SecretKey.fromBytes` runs the §7.2 check on the embedded ek and the §7.3 hash check
(`error.InconsistentKey`); it accepts dk_PKE coefficients ≥ q (FIPS 203 does not check them;
std and OpenSSL accept them too) and reduces them, so `toBytes` of such a key differs from its
input. `decaps` cannot fail (implicit rejection).

## Anchoring

- **External anchor**: NIST ACVP-Server ML-KEM keyGen / encapDecap / key-check vectors
  (`src/testdata/acvp.txt`, US Government work), Wycheproof ML-KEM (`src/testdata/wycheproof.txt`,
  Apache-2.0, see `NOTICE`), the C2SP CCTV modulus vectors (`src/testdata/cctv.txt`, CC0); the
  recipe that extracted them is `tools/vectors/extract.py`. The live oracle `tools/interop.zig`
  (OpenSSL 3.5 libcrypto) and the interop checks of `tools/bench.zig` (OpenSSL and aws-lc-rs, both
  directions). CCTV's unlucky / strcmp / accumulated files were NOT used: they target the FIPS 203
  ipd (KeyGen = G(d), no k byte) and no final-spec implementation reproduces them; Wycheproof's
  regenerated rejection-heavy and strcmp cases cover the same classes.
- **Re-derived**: std's `ml_kem` as a byte-for-byte differential (random seeds, the accumulated
  stream, the fuzz harness), the NTT against a scalar transcription of the pq-crystals reference
  and against schoolbook multiplication, x4 Keccak against std's.

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

## What is deliberately not done

- Kyber round 3 / draft00 — never (superseded by FIPS 203).
- Assembly backends — not now: the portable vector code already beats AWS-LC's AVX2 assembly here;
  revisit only for a target where LLVM's lowering of `@Vector` measurably loses.
- X-Wing / hybrids in this module — never (dependency direction; `hpke`, `tls13`).

## Open

- aarch64 (NEON) speed is unmeasured; the code is portable and tested only on x86-64.
- `KeyPair` and `SecretKey` are large by-value structs (the cached matrix); the `*Into` forms
  avoid the copies, but the std-shaped by-value forms remain.

## Backlog / deferred

- ASN.1 encodings of ML-KEM keys (draft-ietf-lamps-kyber-certificates: `seed`, `expandedKey`,
  `both`; OIDs 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.4.1–3) — in `pkcs8` / `x509`, consuming `seedBytes` and
  `toBytes`.
- A faster scalar Keccak (H(ek) and J(z ‖ c) are 12 serial permutations for ML-KEM-1024 and now the
  largest single cost); std's is used.
- Consumers: switch `tls13`, `hpke`, `dtls`, `tlsclient` from std `ml_kem` to this module (each
  needs its own delta audit afterwards).
